utterances.text: -- That's -- if it would be that easy, Mr. Guy-Smith, then it would be easy to write a judgement. Just listen to what the witness tells you who is innocent and who is guilty and just repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have full confidence that it's not easy to write a judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. But before we do so, Mr. Kearney, could I just seek one clarification. You told us about what the FARK member said about the fish in Lake Radoniq. You then said: "I refer to" -- I think you said people that were missing. Did he, apart from talking about the fish, did he ever refer to people that had disappeared or went missing or was it just you who made that link between his comments and what you apparently had heard about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. With the exception to the reference to the fish in Lake Radoniq, he did not say anything specific. But as I was asked, I was trying to interpret what he meant and this was from what I knew and what the information that was going around was. But I could not get into his head to know exactly what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, in paragraph 101, Witness 17, you say: "He asked for the KLA to be disciplined and well-behaved and to stop committing these crimes." My question to you is: Was he -- did he specifically mention the KLA when he was discussing the fish getting fat in Lake Radoniq?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: It's the -- he was calling for the -- those irresponsible people to be disciplined and to stop committing crimes, and as I said in line with the information that we had and with what we knew, and we knew who was detained at that point, in those moments, and they, the people who were detained, have referred to the KLA as being the perpetrator, the KLA having detained them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But when he was directing his remarks at the irresponsible people to be disciplined and stop committing crimes, did he specifically reference people within the KLA at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: No. As I said, it was a call to those irresponsible people to stop. He did not go into specifics and to mentioning names. He didn't give any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But -- and we understand that he didn't mention specific names, but the irresponsible people he was referring to were members of what organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I think I said this earlier. With regard to what we knew about the disappearance of people, those irresponsible people were members of the KLA on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When this statement was said, was it -- was it loud enough for people in the room to hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: The discussion that takes place in such a meeting is organised and takes place in such a way for everyone present to hear what is meant by what is said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What was Ramush Haradinaj's reaction, if any, to this comment being made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: There was no reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did anyone in the room object to that statement or deny the allegation made by that FARK member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: No, because at that time there was a very delicate subject to talk about these things. So no comments were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you say it was a delicate subject, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: People feared to raise these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Were you afraid to raise these issues as well, Witness 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: To discuss them in -- to raise them openly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: You must understand at a meeting where -- which is attended by more than a hundred representatives, it's not logical even to discuss details such as those, but we worked through other channels to raise these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why was it not logical to discuss details -- those details openly in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: But you got to think about the reprisals that could follow, in this sense I think it was not logical to raise them. And you had to come up with something very specific to raise this. So we were still at an investigative phase and we could not yet come up with the specific charges. There were indications, but we had not been able to firm up facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you say that reprisals could follow if you mentioned these things openly, what do you mean by that, that reprisals could follow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: By analysing the incidents that we were involved in since our entry into Kosovo up until that moment. It was not the appropriate moment to raise these issues which could -- which could bring about an aggravation of the relations, especially at the moment when we had set up this Joint Command and we had started to work together. And it wasn't the time to look at these issues, but it would be better to work together and come to conclusions together, conclusions together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to my last area of inquiry, if I may, at this time. This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one matter of clarification, the last answer. When the witness says it would be better to work together and come to conclusions together," I wonder if he might explain what the word "together" means, together with whom would he and the leadership been working to investigate these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, although the question could have been put in cross-examination perhaps it clarifies the examination-in-chief. Could you answer that question with whom work together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was clear to me what this meant, but for those persons who were responsible in Kosova, I don't know if you can hear me. It was clear to me but for those persons who were engaged in activities in Kosova whether they did not receive these information or refused to receive this information that we had. We had a meeting before entering Kosova in Oslo and we agreed on establishing a Joint Command. This was around 23rd or 24th of May, this meeting. This command was supposed to carry the name of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Kosova, shortly FARK, and it was supposed to include all the units of the KLA and the Territorial Defence. This was an agreement that was reached between the political representative of the KLA and the defence minister of the Republic of Kosova at the meeting in Oslo. So I was not clear whether this information had reached those in charge in Kosova or whether they simply refused to receive this information. We always tried in all possible ways for the Oslo agreement to be implemented from the moment we enter Kosova. That's why I'm saying that "together" means cooperation between the FARK and the KLA, a Joint Command that would be Operational Staff in the Dukagjini Plain, while the representative of this command or the person in charge in this command was Tahir Zemaj. First it came out as a proposal, as a demand, of the villages, and later on it was realised in concrete terms. So the villagers proposed for Tahir Zemaj to become the commander of the Dukagjini Plain staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Emmerson was -- question was more limited. When you said -- do I understand that when you refer to working together, that you meant that not in such a huge meeting but in your future close cooperation between FARK and KLA, that you would deal with these kind of matters as well. Is that how I have to understand it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The establishment of the Joint Command after the 20th of August had this goal, and this was our goal from the moment we entered Kosova up to that time and even later on. The disagreements, the incidents that followed, delayed this establishment and had a negative impact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I'm -- you're entering the last area of your examination-in-chief or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that will certainly take a couple of minutes, I take it. Then perhaps we should first -- unless you say it's a matter of three, four minutes, then we could continue; otherwise, I would like to take a break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: It's a three- or four-minute line of inquiry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But perhaps it's better, more natural to have a pause between the start of the cross-examination and examination-in-chief. So, therefore, please continue but try to finish within the next-- not more than the next three to four minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 17, the last area of inquiry I have for you is related to paragraph 66 of your statement. In that paragraph you state - and I'm quoting. "around this time-period, July of 1998, I began to hear talk from villagers and soldiers of people arrested by the KLA 'being sent to Gllogjan.' My understanding based on these discussions was that those who were sent to Gllogjan hardly ever came back." I'd like to ask you, if you could, to tell the Trial Chamber in more detail where you heard this phrase "being sent to Gllogjan" first of all.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I visited the entire region after I arrived in Kosova. I visited the regional headquarters of the villages, and each and every commander and each and every staff was informed by me about the purpose of our arrival there, about the way the army was organised, and about the future tasks and restructuring. So during these meetings that I had with these representatives of operative units, I heard such information on things that I've mentioned in my statement. I cannot speak in concrete terms because I had just arrived in that area, and I did not know many people except for these two persons that I usually held contact with. But as time went by, I started to get to know people better in that area. So this was the atmosphere that prevailed and how we discussed these matters. But again I would like to say that we did not discuss them in concrete terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But that phrase, "being sent to Gllogjan" was told to you by people in operative KLA units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: By people who had been part of regional commands, village commands, up to that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How many times did you hear this phrase from people in village commands, about being sent to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: It was enough to hear it once, as far as I'm concerned; but I cannot tell you the exact number, how many times I heard it. In other words, I want to say that I heard this phrase at least once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: The second part of your statement in that paragraph: "My understanding based on these discussions was that those who were sent to Gllogjan hardly ever came back," where did you learn that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I already told you earlier that I got this information during my visits to the villages because I maintained contact with the area of responsibility, and this was daily contact depending on the combat activities. But I can say that at least I visited one village per day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And this information about people hardly ever coming back from Gllogjan once they were sent there, can you estimate for the Trial Chambers how many times you heard that information during these visits you made?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I already told you that I cannot pin-point a number, but at least once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And when you say "at least once," is the actual number or is it one time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to object at this time because it's asking for speculation and lacks strength it's also been asked and answered on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, that's -- "at least" is possibly more than once but not necessarily. I mean, that question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, with that, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to seek one or two -- you said that you understood that those who were sent to Gllogjan hardly ever came back, which suggests that you got information of people not coming back but not always. Do you remember any information that people did come back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where -- when did you learn this? In a conversation with whom as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I got this information from my contacts with Din Krasniqi. He was the commander of Lugu i Baranit before the operative units arrived there. It is about a certain Zenun, who was believed to have been sent there and with my intervention that nothing should happen to him but he should return, I know that measures were undertaken and that this person came back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did you ever have a conversation about persons being sent to Gllogjan with anyone who specified the person that was sent to Gllogjan? So, for example, to say, my father was sent to Gllogjan or my uncle or -- I mean, not in general terms discussing people being sent to, but person A or person B, do you remember any such conversation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were such conversations, for example, the one with the brother of Sanije Balaj. He visited the command on many occasions trying to find out where his sister was. There were occasions when he just said, I just want to know where her bones are so that we can bury them according to our traditions. So such conversations did occur on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you were earlier referring to the category of people being sent to Gllogjan. Was that line introduced in that conversation or are you talking about a person not necessarily linked to being sent to Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, not in concrete terms because when I visited these villages I was in the beginning of my activities. I didn't know so many people so I couldn't enter into conversation with just anybody. But as time went by and as the structures and the operative units were set up, there was a person in charge who was appointed for this particular task to collect information through conversations with people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But where you talked about this brother coming and asking about the whereabouts of his sister, is -- do you have any recollection of similar conversations where someone came and said this person disappeared or was sent to Gllogjan or in whatever language he used, do you remember any similar conversation -- conversations of a similar character?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, except for Sanije Balaj's brother, who visited very often.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to seek one matter of clarification arising from the question that Your Honour asked in relation to the Sanije Balaj incident and the report from the brother. It wasn't entirely clear to me from the testimony, and certainly not from the 92 ter or previous statements, whether the witness is suggesting that Sanije Balaj's brother reported to him that Sanije Balaj had been taken to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's a question that could be put to the witness. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The reason I ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- is because Your Honour's supplementary question seemed from the assumption that there might be other examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When the brother of Sanije Balaj came to you, did he just ask about the whereabouts of his sister or did he say, I would like to know where she is because she was sent to Gllogjan? Did he -- I did understand that he not necessarily used that phrase that she was sent to Gllogjan, but rather that she disappeared. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will explain it if you wish in greater details, but I can do this in private session because certain names will be mentioned and I wouldn't like to speak about those persons in an open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I -- however, I suggest that we do that after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I'm happy to do it in the course of cross-examination when the matter arises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could give an opportunity right at the beginning so it's fresh in the recollection of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact, I was seeking a very specific clarification of a particular point that was suggested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If that's not clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's clear that the witness has an explanatory answer he wants to give to the question of the Trial Chambers. I would ask permission to have him give that answer before cross-examination starts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that's the proper way to proceed, but we'll do that after the break. Witness 17, we'll have a break for -- until ten minutes past 1.00, and then we'll resume in private session right away to give you an opportunity to further explain your last answer.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Witness 17, you'll now be cross-examined. May I take it, Mr. Emmerson, that you're the first one to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 17, I want to start, if I may, please, by asking you some questions about the early stages of the entry of the officers with whom you and Tahir Zemaj entered Kosova. First of all, your understanding --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Tahir Zemaj his name is, not Tahir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think I said Zemaj. Your understanding was that there had been an agreement reached in Oslo during May between representatives of the government in exile and representatives of the KLA General Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I don't think, but I can assert here that there was an agreement because I was indirectly involved in that meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, would you take care to switch off your microphone when the witness answers a question in view of the voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you know who the KLA General Staff were, that is to say, what the membership of the KLA General Staff was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Are you talking about the Oslo meeting or in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm speaking more generally. Did you -- were you aware at the time that this agreement was made of who comprised the KLA General Staff at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I said it earlier, that there was a political representative of the KLA who represented the KLA in Oslo, it was Mr. Adem Demaqi, and also a member of the General Staff of the KLA known by the alias of Zeka. These two people had talks with Ahmet Krasniqi, the defence minister, and his deputy Agim Mehmeti, and the meeting took place in Oslo. That was between the 22nd and the 24th of May, 1998. Zekaj was the alias of the person who I can mention the full name is Xhavit Haliti.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Apart from Adem Demaqi and Xhavit Haliti, did you have any information about the structure or membership of the so-called General Staff of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: At the time when we're talking about the Oslo agreement and the talks between the 22nd and 24th of May, 1998, I knew nothing about who was a member of the general staff of the KLA, and that's with the exception of these two people who initiated this meeting and who participated at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So apart from what these two people said at the meeting, you had no means of knowing whether they were representative of KLA forces on the ground or in communication with KLA forces on the ground. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it that way because the organisation of this meeting was done by people who were responsible and who knew both Ahmet Krasniqi and Adem Demaqi, and it was through these people that this meeting and agreement was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your understanding it was that there was to be created an integrated force under the name and insignia of the KLA when you entered Kosovo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: A Joint Command was to be formed which would be called the Armed Forces of the Republic of Kosova, whereas the KLA would be the gist of that force. And according to that agreement, it was thought not to change the name of KLA because this name meant something to the population. The war had already started, and the Joint Command would be the Joint Command with -- of a force, the bulk of which would come from the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And so as you envisaged it at the time you crossed into Kosovo, on the ground there would be no distinction between the two forces. They would all call themselves KLA and all be part of the KLA. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: According to the Oslo agreement, after that agreement the staff of the armed forces of the defence ministry was set up in Tirana, and under the umbrella of that staff there would be representatives of the General Staff of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You knew, presumably, when you entered Kosovo that the area of Kosovo that you were entering was the Dukagjini Zone or the Dukagjini area, western Kosovo, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As far as you are aware, did Tahir Zemaj or any of the other senior commanders send an advanced party to establish communication with the leadership of the KLA that was already operating on the ground in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: This was the responsibility of the defence minister of Kosovo, Ahmet Krasniqi, and Adem Demaqi, who at that time did not come out in public because he was living in Pristina. They had the task of informing the groups who were operating in Kosovo, they would inform the people on the qualities and the contents of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And presumably you have no information one way or the other as to whether or not they did, in fact, communicate the agreement to those on the ground in western Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Today I think I mentioned that, as far as I remember, that it was not clear to us whether this agreement had reached each person in charge in each and every area that the defence ministry units and the KLA had reached an agreement or whether the agreement had reached them; but they did not want to implement it, that agreement. I'm talking about that time, not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, and to make it clear, all the questions I'm asking you are also about your knowledge at that time, Witness 17. Does it follow from the answers that you've given then that nobody was sent by Tahir Zemaj or the commanders of the officers who were to enter Kosovo on the -- in the second half of June, that nobody was sent by them to make contact and communicate with the KLA commanders into whose area you were about to march?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: According to us, there was no need to duplicate things to send somebody else -- to send somebody else in addition to the people who were tasked with going out to all the areas and inform people about the agreement. We did not want to come out of what was said and agreed at the meeting; on the contrary, we tried to implement every point as was agreed at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I think in your witness statement you mention three early meetings that took place. I'm just going to remind you of what they were. First of all you say - and these are all meetings that took place incidentally before your march from Jasic to Isniq. You describe first of all, a meeting on the 25th of June in Jasic at which Sali Veseli and Naim Maloku spoke to you and Tahir Zemaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And certainly from what they said they did not appear to know about the existence of the Oslo agreement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: On the basis of the conversation with Tahir Zemaj about the -- the people responsible at the time in Kosovo, namely Sali Veseli and Naim Maloku, it turns out that they said that they had no knowledge about any agreement and the arrival of the Operational Staff units in Kosovo. But they said that they were going to be informed about this agreement, about this new structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The next meeting that you describe as having taken place the following day, the 26th of June, at Jasic, when Mr. Haradinaj attended and both Sali Veseli and Naim Maloku were present again and there were further discussions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Yes, the discussions continued and this was because of the disagreement surrounding our entering Kosova and the way it was misinterpreted by certain persons who were operating in Dukagjini area. That's why we continued with our discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you describe in your witness statement Mr. Haradinaj in that meeting of the 26th of June, you describe him as being controlled and orderly. Is that an accurate description?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Yes, a very accurate description. He was a very constructive, moderate, this is the impression I got.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were asked by Judge Orie some questions about the nature of the disagreement. Does it come to this, that Mr. Haradinaj was in effect saying: We have forces on the ground already located and defending villages, and what we need to you to do is to distribute your officers and soldiers in order to fortify the defences that already exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: The disagreement was that, that he asked for the senior officers to be distributed in the operative units and in the villages and to carry out their tasks within the structure of the Dukagjini operative staff; however, we were already an established military structure under the command of the Ministry of Defence. These were the frictions that continued. We were not in a position to do such a thing, to systemize 23 senior officers to destroy our own structure and enter the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But in summary, Witness 17, those first two meetings on the 25th and the 26th, although of course there were differences of opinion between the two sides, they were constructive discussions about how to move forward and accommodate the new force. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Of course, we were not crazy. Both sides were ready to reach an agreement; however, none of the sides wanted to change its views, to abandon its positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your witness statement you go on to describe a further meeting that took place in Junik on the 30th of June which you attended, together with others, on behalf of the newly arrived force and Sali Veseli attended on behalf of the KLA. You remember that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in your witness statement - this is paragraph 18 - don't bother to turn it up, you say that during the course of that meeting you said, that is you personally said, that if anybody obstructed your march to Isniq, then - and these are your words - "we would have to act according to military rules." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I was passing the words of my commander, that is, that we have entered Kosova and we are implementing the second phase. The first phase was positions at Jasic and the second was to go to Isniq, while the third to establish the barracks. So I just passed on his words, that we must fulfil, implement, the second phase; and if we see any obstacles as military persons, we would act.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so we're clear you were in effect saying that: If anybody gets in our way, we will shoot them, is that correct, we will take military action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I don't know how you're interpreting my answer, but we made it clear to them that it was a must for us to implement the second phase. That did not mean that we would open fire, but the army had to carry out its tasks and implement it plans. So we made it clear to them that we had to go there and implement the second phase and that it would be nice if there were no incidents accompanying the second phase. Later it was a way -- it was implemented. We didn't have any incidents when we travelled from Junik to Isniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I understand that and I'm asking these questions to you, Witness 17, for a reason. You say in your statement that you explicitly told Mr. Veseli that if there was obstruction you would "act according to military rules." Now, do I understand that correctly to mean that if you were obstructed in your passage you would take military action against those obstructing you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Let me speak in more concrete terms. We were told clearly to systemize in the villages to become part of the structures, existing structures, in Kosova, or to go back because there was no place for us there. So that's why it was necessary to make it clear to them that we have an agreement, we have a command, we have a goal, we are in a phase that needs to be completed, and we have to reach our destination. This is the military language that should be understood in this way. We had an order that needed to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's, I hope, a direct enough question, Witness 17, and I'd like if you would, please, just to answer it yes or no. I'm going to read to you the words of your statement where you tell us what you said to Mr. Veseli, and it says this, you said that: "If anyone got in our way then we would have to act according to military rules." And my question is: When you were threatening action according to military rules if anybody got in your way, were you threatening to take military action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: This is not a threat, rather, an explanation, detailed explanation about the order that we have as an organised unit with its respective command. We had to show to the existing forces in Kosovo the reason why we were there, who had sent us there. So it's not a threat, it's an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That night, the 30th of June, the march was effective, was it not; in other words, overnight you and the soldiers and officers with whom you had come crossed over from Jasic to Isniq. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, prior to that time you say certainly from the KLA side there had been no threats of the use of military force against you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: We had an ultimatum either to join or become part of their command or go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You describe in your statement a meeting on the 2nd of July in Isniq at which a man called Rrustem Tetaj was present and Mr. Haradinaj present as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I don't know where you got Mr. Haradinaj's name as a person attending this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'll return to your statement in a moment or two and it may be to do with the way in which I've read it. But you record at paragraph 24 in your statement Mr. Tetaj having told you at that meeting on the 2nd of July that the KLA Dukagjin staff had been formed in Jabllanice on the 23rd of May, 1998. And I'm going to suggest to you that you are wrong about what you have recorded there, either you're wrong about the date or you are confusing two meetings because we have seen documentation of meetings relating to May and June. And I want to suggest to you that the first formed Dukagjin staff was formed on the 23rd of May in Gllogjan and not in Jabllanice. Now, could you be mistaken in that passage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/17
utterances.text: I was saying what Rrustem Tetaj told me at that time. He said that a meeting was held and that the staff was established in Jabllanice on that date. Now, whether it coincides or whether it was planned to be that way, the date coincides with a date of the meeting in Oslo between the KLA representatives and the representatives of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's simply the location I'm concerned about at the moment, Witness 17, and we're shortly to adjourn. Can I ask you this, please: You had available to you at the time that you made your witness statement the notebook that is appended as annex 1, and I'm going to suggest to you that where you deal with this meeting you have recorded the date of the 23rd but not the place of the meeting that was relayed to you by Rrustem Tetaj as the place where the operative staff had formed. And I want to again, in light of the fact that you were using your notes, ask you, perhaps overnight, to consider whether or not you may be mistaken in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we'll do at this moment is we will adjourn. I take it that my words are still -- there's no possibility to hear me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters cannot hear anything from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn and first thing tomorrow morning we'll do is to establish in open court that there was a problem with the electricity and that therefore the transcript, even of the words I'm speaking at this very moment, is not available. Counsel for the accused are invited to communicate this to their clients who could not understand what I'm saying at this moment. Witness 17, could you take off your earphones. Can you understand me in the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, as you have given it today and as you will continue to give it tomorrow. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in another courtroom, that is, Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll put on the record tomorrow what happened at the end of today. Would you please remain seated until, since the protective measures are still in place. I would urge the parties not to say anything that should be recorded because it will not be on the transcript and it will be lost and to keep it for tomorrow morning, 9.00, Courtroom 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of August, 2007, at 9.00 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
